goal: Within ONE scheduler step, submit an eager EXTEND sub-forward for the admitted prefill chunk PLUS a decode CUDA-graph-replay sub-forward, back-to-back on the forward stream, so decode advances every step of a prefill wave instead of stalling for the whole wave (measured: 47 serialized prefill forwards at 867ms steal 33.8% of wall; enable_mixed_chunk demotes decode to eager 36.9ms median vs 22ms graph).

One ScheduleBatch per step flows to run_batch; NextBatchPlan (schedule_batch.py:4138-4140) carries only batch_to_run + running_batch.

2_why_mixed_goes_eager: Gate 1 (graph eligibility): _forward_raw computes mode_check = forward_batch.forward_mode.is_cuda_graph() (model_runner.py:1986-1990) and can_run_graph = mode_check() and self.decode_cuda_graph_runner and ...can_run_graph(forward_batch) (model_runner.py:1991-1995). ForwardMode.is_cuda_graph (model_executor/forward_batch_info.py:275-281) returns True only for DECODE / TARGET_VERIFY / IDLE / DLLM_EXTEND -- MIXED is NOT in the list, so a MIXED batch can never reach decode_cuda_graph_runner.execute (model_runner.py:2006-2011) and falls through to the eager path (model_runner.py:2062-2065, self.eager_runner.execute).

Gate 2 (eager demotion): EagerRunner.execute (model_executor/runner/eager_runner.py:210) explicitly rewrites forward_batch.forward_mode = ForwardMode.EXTEND when mode.is_mixed() (eager_runner.py:215-221, comment: 'A mixed batch is extend-shaped (decode tails are 1-token extends)') and dispatches _execute_extend (eager_runner.py:222-226). This is where the measured 38.5->36.9ms decode slowdown comes from: decode rows run as eager 1-token extends inside an 8192-token eager extend forward instead of a 22ms captured decode graph.

Not rescued by prefill graphs either: the piecewise prefill-graph branch requires forward_mode.is_extend(...) and self.prefill_cuda_graph_runner.can_run_graph(forward_batch) (model_runner.py:2036-2043, condition at :2040); is_extend() does include MIXED (forward_batch_info.py:213-220) but prefill graphs are token-bucket keyed for extend shapes and the decode rows make the batch ineligible in practice -- consistent with the measured eager medians.

Root cause summary: graphs are captured per (bs) ShapeKey for DECODE-shaped forwards only (decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1249-1332), and the MIXED mode flag itself is the disqualifier at model_runner.py:1986-1995; nothing ever captures a graph keyed for a mixed batch, and nothing replays the decode graph for the decode subset of a mixed batch.

3_composition_plan.design: Stop merging decode reqs INTO the prefill batch. Keep two ScheduleBatch objects per step: (A) new_batch stays a pure EXTEND batch (never call mix_with_running, so it never becomes MIXED and stays on the existing eager extend path -- same kernels as a non-mixed prefill step), and (B) running_batch.prepare_for_decode() (schedule_batch.py:3736) as a pure DECODE batch that goes through the EXISTING graph-replay path unchanged (is_cuda_graph passes, bucket-padded replay). Submit both to the GPU back-to-back within one scheduler iteration.
steps: A. Batch construction (scheduler.py get_new_batch_prefill, replace the mix block at scheduler.py:4471-4505): keep the guard list (4471-4483) and the finishing-req filter (4481-4483) and check_decode_mem (4488); call running_batch.prepare_for_decode() (4489, unchanged call); DELETE the mix_with_running call (4490-4491) and the empty-standin swap (4503-4505). Return the decode batch via a new optional NextBatchPlan field decode_batch (NextBatchPlan msgspec Struct at schedule_batch.py:4138-4140 -- add field with default None; msgspec handles optional fields). plan.running_batch stays the real running_batch object (mutated in place by prepare_for_decode), so the next step's last-extend-batch merge (scheduler.py:3988-4004) re-attaches prefill survivors exactly like a non-mixed prefill step, and decode rows were already advanced by the decode sub-forward.

B. Dispatch (scheduler.py get_next_batch_to_run 4049-4063 + both loops): when a prefill batch is chosen (ret = new_batch) and plan.decode_batch is non-empty, keep ret = prefill batch and thread the companion. In event_loop_overlap (scheduler.py:2166) and event_loop_normal (scheduler.py:2105): batch_result_prefill = self.run_batch(prefill); batch_result_decode = self.run_batch(decode_batch); append/process both. Two forward calls per step are already supported by the runner API: ModelRunner.forward is call-scoped (per-call forward_pass_id increment at model_runner.py:1824; fresh forward_context per call inside _forward_raw, model_runner.py:1963-1975; expert recorder keyed by forward_pass_id). No model_executor file changes -- the decode sub-forward is literally today's decode path.

C. Streams: both run_batch calls execute under self.forward_stream_ctx with forward_stream.wait_stream(schedule_stream) (scheduler.py:4782-4799) -- SAME forward stream, so CUDA serializes the 867ms eager prefill kernels and the 22ms decode graph replay; the decode replay launch is enqueued immediately after the prefill launch (host-side enqueue ~us), so decode never idles waiting for a scheduler round-trip: it executes the moment prefill drains. v1 rejects two-stream overlap: graph ShapeKey carries a stream_idx only under pdmux (decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:876-884), and cross-stream replay would race req_to_token_pool writes and per-stream attn metadata; the stolen 33.8% is decode IDLE, not missing FLOP overlap, so same-stream piggyback recovers it.

D. Sampling and outputs: each sub-batch keeps its own per-batch sampling -- tp_worker builds delay_sample_func (tp_worker.py:732-741) under overlap or samples inline (tp_worker.py:744-747); scheduler launch_batch_sample_if_needed (scheduler.py:5139) fires once per batch_result, and it is called with the CURRENT step's batch_result per iteration (scheduler.py:2181-2183 area), so extend to fire for both results in order. The two req sets are disjoint, so inter-batch sampling order is semantically free; intra-batch order is byte-identical to today. process_batch_result / BatchResultProcessor then sees a plain EXTEND batch and a plain DECODE batch: the mixed-only classification branches (batch_result_processor.py:374-395 keyed on batch.decoding_reqs membership; metrics_reporter.py:448-468 keyed on forward_mode.is_mixed()) simply take their non-mixed paths, which is exactly the semantics a non-mixed server produces -- numerics per request are the same kernels in the same order (prefill: eager _execute_extend, decode: captured graph replay), just co-issued.

E. Overlap bookkeeping: result_queue gets two appends per iteration (pattern at scheduler.py:2169); _reqs_finishing_inflight asserts len(self.result_queue) == 1 (scheduler.py:4539-4542) and pop_and_process pops one per iteration (scheduler.py:2129-2131). Cheapest correct handling: when a companion decode batch ran, process the prefill result synchronously at end of the same iteration (mirroring the disable_overlap_for_batch early pop at scheduler.py:2152-2158) and keep the decode result as the single overlapped entry; set self.last_batch = decode_batch (scheduler.py:2188) since running_batch identity already holds those reqs. Alternative (stage 2): relax the queue to depth 2 and make _reqs_finishing_inflight scan both entries.

F. KV/allocator: total allocation identical to today's mixed step -- prefill allocates its chunk slots, decode allocates 1 bonus slot per running req, same pools, same allocator, same stream (no cross-stream allocator hazard). Decode replay allocates nothing at replay time (static buffers filled by buffer_registry.fill_from, decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1676-1686 via load_batch). Radix/tree-cache semantics return to non-mixed behavior: prefill rows checkpoint, decode rows release-on-finish via the plain paths (batch_result_processor.py:374-395), removing the decoding_reqs suppression the mixed path needed. The prefill admission budget accounting for decode rows (scheduler.py:4260) stays as-is so the adder still reserves decode memory headroom.
numerics_guards: T1 greedy A/B equality: identical request stream, fixed seed, greedy sampling, composition ON vs composition OFF (plain alternation); assert token-for-token identical outputs and identical finish reasons. This is the strongest proof that per-request kernels/order are unchanged.

T2 CPU unit (mocked ScheduleBatch): with composition on, get_new_batch_prefill returns an EXTEND batch with decoding_reqs None and forward_mode == EXTEND (never MIXED), plus a DECODE companion whose input_ids come from the plain decode path (output_ids[-1]) -- and resolve_forward_inputs' mixed branch (overlap_utils.py:121-142) is not taken for composed steps.

T3 runtime evidence: SGLANG_LOG_DECODE_GRAPH_KEY=1 (decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:1994-2005) must log a decode graph replay during every prefill-wave step; device_timer spans (profile_range at model_runner.py:1831-1839; decode vs extend categories) must show prefill and decode spans adjacent within one scheduler iteration.
T4 invariant hook: debug-mode assert that _forward_raw never receives forward_mode == MIXED when composition is enabled (would catch any residual mix_with_running path).

4_risks_and_fallbacks: R1 overlap scheduler assumes ONE batch per step (result_queue depth and pop_and_process pairing, scheduler.py:2129-2131/2169; single last_batch slot, scheduler.py:2188; _reqs_finishing_inflight len==1 assert, scheduler.py:4539-4542). Cheapest fallback: ship v1 for event_loop_normal only (scheduler.py:2083 -- synchronous result processing, no queue, no assert) and feature-detect overlap mode off; stage 2 implements the paired-pop of step E.

R2 output processing and metrics key on mixed classification (batch.decoding_reqs membership in batch_result_processor.py:374-395; forward_mode.is_mixed() per-batch split in metrics_reporter.py:448-468) and on one result per step. Cheapest fallback: tag the decode sub-batch with decoding_reqs = self.reqs (the schedule_batch.py:3400 pattern) and the extend sub-batch with decoding_reqs = [] so every existing branch classifies each req exactly as the mixed batch did; the per-batch reporter branches already handle plain decode/extend batches.

R3 spec / DP-attention / pipeline interactions: spec v2 publishes mid-worker via on_publish per step (scheduler.py:4789-4796); require_mlp_sync couples decode-graph eligibility to global sync (model_runner.py:1996-2000 can_run_decode_cuda_graph gate inside can_run_graph); verify graphs key on num_tokens_per_req width (decode_cuda_graph_runner.py:866-873); PP passes pp_proxy_tensors between stages. Cheapest fallback: guard composition to spec_algorithm.is_none() and not require_mlp_sync and not dp-attention and pp_size == 1 (add to the existing guard list at scheduler.py:4471-4483) -- exactly the measured C32 single-replica config; everything else keeps today's behavior. The existing _should_defer_prefill admission throttle (scheduler.py:1457/4029, commit 2a638ba) is orthogonal and stays: it only matters when composition declines a step.

expected_effect_honest: Same-stream composition does NOT overlap FLOPs: per prefill step wall becomes 867ms + 22ms (+2.5%). What it removes is the decode STALL: today 'Run prefill first if possible' (scheduler.py:4049-4051) means decode makes zero progress across an entire 47-forward prefill wave (the measured 33.8% stolen wall); composed, decode advances one token per <=889ms throughout the wave on its captured 22ms graph (vs 36.9ms eager with enable_mixed_chunk, and vs worker A's defer-one-step swap which bounds but does not eliminate stalls). Worst-case inter-token gap during waves drops from wave-length (seconds) to chunk_time + 22ms.
